measured_matches.note: Measured with scripts/discovery-week-score-2026-09-22.ts: grants_with_funder rows for this source, normaliseScrapedGrant, computeMatchScore, floor 55. 'structure' is whether the staged row lists the org's legal_structure.

rows: ECB Building Belonging in Cricket Fund 87

measurement_findings: Every small local fund staged here scores 15 to 35 for the org it was found for, not 55+. Two causes, both in the matcher rather than the tagging. First, grantSize scores 2 of 10 with the label 'Grant size — below your minimum' whenever the award is under the org's stated minimum, which is true of every £250 to £3,000 community foundation fund. Second, a borough-tagged row scores 2 of 15 on location for an org whose primary_location is the city: Funding Differently (location_tag 'Southwark') scores 15 for Paws and Pause, whose profile says 'LONDON'. The row's tag matches the catalogue convention (every held Southwark, Lambeth and Islington row is tagged by borough), so the fix is the org profile or the matcher, not the row.

The consequence for Tuesday's digest: the rows that will actually surface as new matches are the national, no-maximum trusts, not the local funds. Funding Differently is the single best new fund for Paws and Pause on the page and it will not surface at 55.

Control: the score spread across all 16 staged rows for Bridlington Cricket Foundation is 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, 15, 44, 44, 61, 61, 61, 61, 87 — the floor does exclude, so the counts above are not a scorer that passes everything.
reopenings_note: No held row could be given a dated reopening. Every closed fund walked either gave no date ('Autumn 2026', 'later this year', 'check back later') or a season without a day ('Opening Spring 2027'). Two Ridings, London Community Foundation and Suffolk Community Foundation were the three community foundations most likely to yield one and all three were fully deduped: every open fund they list is already held.
